about.description:
ccusage reads the local session logs written by coding agent CLIs -- Claude
Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and others -- and reports the
tokens they consumed and what those tokens cost. Reports can be grouped by
day, week, month, session or billing block, printed as tables or JSON, and
rendered as a compact status line for Claude Code hooks.
about.summary: Analyze coding (agent) CLI token usage and costs from local data

content:
upstream_rev=$(sed -n '/^    "litellm": {/,/^    }/p' "${SRC_DIR}/flake.lock" | sed -n 's/^ *"rev": "\([0-9a-f]\{40\}\)".*/\1/p')
if [ -z "${upstream_rev}" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: no nodes.litellm.locked.rev in ${SRC_DIR}/flake.lock." >&2
  echo "Upstream may no longer pin the LiteLLM pricing snapshot through its flake." >&2
  echo "Check how this tag obtains the snapshot and update the recipe to match." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ "${upstream_rev}" != "${{ litellm_rev }}" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: the vendored LiteLLM pricing snapshot is stale." >&2
  echo "  litellm_rev in recipe.yaml: ${{ litellm_rev }}" >&2
  echo "  nodes.litellm.locked.rev:   ${upstream_rev}" >&2
  echo "Set litellm_rev to ${upstream_rev} and refresh the pricing source sha256 with:" >&2
  echo "  curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/${upstream_rev}/model_prices_and_context_window.json | sha256sum" >&2
  exit 1
fi

raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "20.0.20"
  # nodes.litellm.locked.rev from the upstream flake.lock of this tag
  litellm_rev: 1a183efaa1a2108aed7e1bed8d445d93bd1aa60d

package:
  name: ccusage
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  - url: https://github.com/ccusage/ccusage/archive/refs/tags/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: 24f81ac3dc5ca049b4170256402d67675fe7c2aa084274326726acf5cfcc8428
  # The build embeds a LiteLLM pricing snapshot. Vendoring it as a source and
  # pointing CCUSAGE_PRICING_JSON_PATH at it keeps the build offline and avoids
  # the `fetch-litellm-pricing` feature, whose minreq/rustls/aws-lc-sys
  # build-dependency does not cross-compile. The build script fails if a version
  # bump leaves litellm_rev behind the rev upstream pins in flake.lock.
  - url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/${{ litellm_rev }}/model_prices_and_context_window.json
    sha256: a74538d2edc13e1eb4f67870fbc2ee05035326e6eaed0dc5bce11d372cff6e60
    file_name: model_prices_and_context_window.json

build:
  number: 1
  script:
    env:
      CCUSAGE_PRICING_JSON_PATH: ${{ "$SRC_DIR/model_prices_and_context_window.json" if unix else "%SRC_DIR%\\model_prices_and_context_window.json" }}
    content:
      # litellm_rev is pinned independently of ${{ version }}, so a version bump
      # can leave it behind and silently embed stale prices. flake.lock is
      # upstream's source of truth for the revision, so compare against it.
      - if: unix
        then:
          - |
            upstream_rev=$(sed -n '/^    "litellm": {/,/^    }/p' "${SRC_DIR}/flake.lock" | sed -n 's/^ *"rev": "\([0-9a-f]\{40\}\)".*/\1/p')
            if [ -z "${upstream_rev}" ]; then
              echo "ERROR: no nodes.litellm.locked.rev in ${SRC_DIR}/flake.lock." >&2
              echo "Upstream may no longer pin the LiteLLM pricing snapshot through its flake." >&2
              echo "Check how this tag obtains the snapshot and update the recipe to match." >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            if [ "${upstream_rev}" != "${{ litellm_rev }}" ]; then
              echo "ERROR: the vendored LiteLLM pricing snapshot is stale." >&2
              echo "  litellm_rev in recipe.yaml: ${{ litellm_rev }}" >&2
              echo "  nodes.litellm.locked.rev:   ${upstream_rev}" >&2
              echo "Set litellm_rev to ${upstream_rev} and refresh the pricing source sha256 with:" >&2
              echo "  curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/${upstream_rev}/model_prices_and_context_window.json | sha256sum" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
        else:
          # findstr cannot report the new revision, so point at flake.lock instead.
          - 'findstr /c:${{ litellm_rev }} "%SRC_DIR%\flake.lock" >nul || (echo ERROR: litellm_rev is no longer the revision upstream pins in flake.lock, so the vendored LiteLLM pricing snapshot is stale. Set litellm_rev to nodes.litellm.locked.rev from flake.lock and refresh the pricing source sha256. & exit /b 1)'
      # rustc hands the link over to the bundled rust-lld of the x86_64 build
      # host, which does not understand ppc64le relocations. Use the cross
      # toolchain's own linker instead.
      - if: target_platform == "linux-ppc64le"
        then:
          - export CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS="${CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS:-} -C link-self-contained=no -C link-arg=-fuse-ld=bfd"
      - if: unix
        then:
          - cargo auditable install --locked --no-track --bins --root ${{ PREFIX }} --path rust/crates/ccusage
        else:
          - cargo auditable install --locked --no-track --bins --root %LIBRARY_PREFIX% --path rust/crates/ccusage
      - cd rust
      - cargo-bundle-licenses --format yaml --output ../THIRDPARTY.yml

requirements:
  build:
    - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
    - ${{ compiler('c') }}
    - ${{ compiler('rust') }}
    - cargo-auditable
    - cargo-bundle-licenses

tests:
  - script:
      - ccusage --version
      - ccusage --help
      - ccusage daily --help
      - ccusage claude --help
  - package_contents:
      bin:
        - ccusage
      strict: true

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/ccusage/ccusage
  summary: Analyze coding (agent) CLI token usage and costs from local data
  description: |
    ccusage reads the local session logs written by coding agent CLIs -- Claude
    Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and others -- and reports the
    tokens they consumed and what those tokens cost. Reports can be grouped by
    day, week, month, session or billing block, printed as tables or JSON, and
    rendered as a compact status line for Claude Code hooks.
  license: MIT
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
    - apps/ccusage/LICENSE
    - THIRDPARTY.yml
  documentation: https://ccusage.com
  repository: https://github.com/ccusage/ccusage

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - pavelzw
